judged_text: Non-Google calendar services only honor `destinationCalendar[0]`, breaking multi-host collective events for Lark/Office365/CalDAV: `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` (~128, ~164, ~192, ~237) and `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` (~72-76) use the first element as `calendarId`/`eventsUrl`, and `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (~156-166) filters to `externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` — in EventManager's per-destination loop, host B's credential is invoked with host A's calendar, causing API errors or silent no-ops so host B silently gets no event.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, but it passes the same `event` object containing the full `destinationCalendar` array each time. Non-Google calendar services in this diff (e.g., `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, and `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`) explicitly destructure only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and use that for `calendarId`/URL filtering. This means when processing later destinations (e.g., host B), these services will still target host A’s calendar externalId, so the event may be created/updated against the wrong calendar or fail (e.g., missing/unauthorized calendar id), resulting in host B not getting their event.
